trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.

Going to number 2 would leave both cell (6,4) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Cell (6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 4; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
Going to number 5 would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (2,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (3,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
